known_facts_book1: One of the birds and animals that fell into the pool of tears with Alice.
Speaks with an important air and uses long words: 'the best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race'.
Marks out a race-course in a sort of circle and sets everyone running with no start and no finish.
Calls out 'The race is over!' after half an hour and declares 'Everybody has won, and all must have prizes.'
Makes Alice supply the prizes from the box of comfits in her pocket, then solemnly presents Alice with her own thimble.
Does not appear again after chapter III.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Turns to her for prizes and hands her back her own thimble with great solemnity.
known_relations_book1.the Mouse: Fellow member of the wet party on the bank; steps in when the Mouse's dry history fails.
known_relations_book1.Lory: Fellow bird in the same party.

not_in_this_book: the Dodo is a friend or ally of Alice
the Dodo appears after the Caucus-race

known_facts_book1: One of the birds in the pool of tears.
Has a long argument with Alice and turns sulky, saying only 'I am older than you, and must know better.'
Refuses to tell its age, which ends the argument.
Shivers and says 'Ugh!' during the Mouse's recitation about William the Conqueror.
Sighs 'What a pity it wouldn't stay!' when the Mouse walks off.

known_relations_book1.Alice: Argues with her about who knows better and refuses to settle it by giving its age.
known_relations_book1.the Mouse: Interrupts its recitation and regrets its departure.

not_in_this_book: the Lory appears after chapter III

known_facts_book1: One of the birds that fell into the pool of tears, listed alongside a Duck, a Dodo and a Lory.
Tells the Dodo 'Speak English! I don't know the meaning of half those long words, and, what's more, I don't believe you do either!' and laughs.
Has no other line and does not appear again.

not_in_this_book: the Eaglet appears after chapter III
